content.comment_body: Hello, I'm interested in purchasing a [product_name] PLC: [article_no], but I'm concerned about potential cybersecurity risks related to the use of a Micro SD card. Is there an option for a similar PLC or an equivalent with integrated internal memory? If a PLC with built-in memory isn't available, are there any solutions—either physical or logical—that could help prevent unauthorized attempts to modify the programs stored on the micro SD card used in the PLC? Regards,

The main cybersecurity risk arises if you connect the [product_name] device to the Internet without proper protection, such as VPN or dynamic DNS services. Programs stored on the SD card can be safeguarded from modification, reading, or deletion using password protection features.

Hi, A [product_name] device can operate without an MSD card. However, you will need an MSD card for: - Running a custom web server - Logging data when you have more than 200 records or multiple data log files All other functions work without the MSD card. Additionally, enhancing security by locking the cabinet can prevent unauthorized physical access. Hope this helps.

Thanks for the information. I'm also concerned about a less common but possible risk: someone taking out the micro SD card, infecting it with malware that activates when plugged into a PC, which then spreads to other networks once the PC is reconnected. I agree that the biggest risk is likely from connecting devices to the Internet without secure measures. My question now is: Is there a way to make the Micro SD card read-only after programming the PLC so it can't be altered?

Thank you for your response; I have considered locking the cabinet, which is a good solution. I apologize for not mentioning earlier that I planned to use a user-defined web server. Your details about system operation without an MSD card are helpful. Do you think a [version_no] with built-in memory would be a suitable alternative to the [product_name] PLC? I am considering this product: [article_no]. It's pricier, but it seems to resolve my concerns. Regards,
I personally am not aware of any method for this.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are focused on cybersecurity risks tied to microSD card usage in [product_name] PLCs, such as the possibility of malware infection through physical card removal and re-insertion. Their discussions touch on features like password protection and locking hardware enclosures, as well as alternatives with integrated memory. Both logical and physical security options are viewed as important parts of the user experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a PLC that either has integrated internal memory or offers strong logical and physical safeguards against unauthorized modifications or malware threats targeting external memory cards.
